key_insight: A locally hosted LLM layered with other detectors offered recall-first and precision-first options for identifying protected health information (PHI) without sending text off-site.
clinical_relevance: The toolkit could support privacy-preserving reuse of clinical text, but its missed-PHI and over-redaction trade-offs require local validation.
method: Combined rule-based detectors, clinical named-entity recognition (NER), and a local 26B mixture-of-experts LLM.
Evaluated recall-first and precision-first configurations against five de-identification tools.
Fixed configurations on tuning halves and evaluated reporting halves using paired patient-level bootstrap intervals.
evidence_signal: Across nursing notes (889 PHI spans) and semi-synthetic discharge summaries (29,023 spans), recall-first sensitivity reached 98.9% and 95.3%, respectively; all four prespecified comparisons held.
watch_item: The discharge-summary advantage over Stanford/Penn arose almost entirely from generated untyped names, limiting inference about performance on real-world clinical names.
paper_title: A local language model layered with rule-based and neural detectors for clinical text de-identification: an open-source toolkit and evaluation
